title: gpu: reduce peak GPU memory and workspace via activation checkpointing, scratch arena, and kernel selection
author: Maya Rodriguez
description: Motivation: Production inference workloads are increasingly constrained by GPU memory headroom and transient workspace allocations. Large-context requests (8k-64k tokens) plus continuous-batching can spike temporary buffer usage and cause OOMs or force degraded scheduling decisions. This PR reduces peak GPU memory and transient workspace pressure by combining three coordinated changes: 1) optional activation checkpointing with configurable granularity and recompute strategy; 2) a scratch buffer arena / pooling layer to avoid frequent cudaMalloc/cudaFree and to reuse temporary workspaces across kernels; 3) improved kernel selection and scheduler heuristics that prefer lower-workspace kernel variants under memory pressure and account for workspace footprint when doing continuous batching and KV-cache routing. Summary of changes (high-level): - Add activation checkpointing primitives to the serving runtime with per-model and per-layer granularity flags. Checkpointing defaults to off for older models but can be enabled via model config and rollout. We implemented a recompute planner that groups layers into checkpoints using a memory/latency tradeoff heuristic (supports target_memory_savings and max_recompute_steps). - Implement a ScratchArena abstraction that preallocates device arenas per GPU stream and reuses scratch buffers for attention, softmax, layernorm, and fused-kernel temporaries. The arena uses binning and a small LRU for large fragments to prevent fragmentation. - Tune arena sizing heuristics using occupancy-aware heuristics: probe occupancy and choose per-GPU arena sizes at init time; expose a runtime flag to scale arena size by percent. - Make kernel selection policy aware of workspace footprint: update the kernel registry to include workspace_bytes metadata and prefer fused kernels that have lower peak workspace when the model or request would otherwise exceed a threshold. - Update continuous-batching scheduler to include workspace budget accounting: batch formation will now subtract estimated workspace from slot budgets to avoid transient OOMs when co-locating requests. - KV cache improvements: avoid duplicative pinned allocations for shared prefix cache by introducing a shared KV region for pinned/common prefixes and add an LRU eviction policy for idle KV segments to reduce retention across long-lived sessions. - Micro-optimizations: reduce temporary tensor allocations in attention path, replace some temporary vector allocations with in-place ops, and avoid unnecessary host-device copies for workspace size negotiation. Testing and safety net: - Extensive unit tests for ScratchArena allocation/free semantics and for activation checkpointing correctness. - Added a regression test workload in perf-canary that simulates continuous-batching with 16 concurrent users and mixed lengths (2k/8k/16k) to assert no OOMs and steady latency. - CI perf jobs added to benchmark memory headroom at 4k/16k/32k contexts. Benchmarks (representative): - 16k context, Llama-2-13B-8bit: peak GPU memory reduced ~22% (from 21.5 GB to ~16.8 GB) with activation checkpointing + arena enabled, workspace transient allocations reduced ~30%. - 8k context, Llama-2-70B quantized: workspace reduction ~25% and tail latency improved 6-8% due to fewer memory stalls. - Continuous-batching throughput unchanged or slightly improved (0-4%) in stable runs; scheduler prevents previously-observed 503s under high-concurrency requests. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind a model-config flag (model.config.enable_workspace_optimizations) and a runtime flag (--enable-scratch-arena, --enable-checkpointing). - Start with internal canary on dedicated clusters, gradual rollout to hosted for opt-in models, then flip defaults for memory-sensitive SKUs after 2 weeks of telemetry. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of ScratchArena and binning algorithm - [x] Activation checkpointing primitives and recompute planner - [x] Kernel registry workspace metadata and selection policy - [x] Scheduler workspace-aware accounting for continuous batching - [x] KV cache shared region and LRU eviction - [x] Unit + integration tests and perf canary harness - [x] Docs and runtime flags documented in runtime/config.md Backwards compatibility: Changes are opt-in; default behavior unchanged unless flags are enabled. Config introduces new fields but they are optional. Risks and mitigations: - Checkpointing increases CPU/GPU compute due to recomputation; planner restricts recompute steps and we provide per-model latency guardrails. - Arena sizing may need tuning on unusual GPU SKUs; runtime flags allow per-cluster overrides. - Kernel selection heuristics could pick slower kernels; selection includes latency_estimate and workspace_bytes scoring to balance tradeoffs. Related work items: ENG-2571 (memory optimization epic), ENG-2634 (continuous-batching improvements), SUP-709 (customer incident that motivated KV cache duplication fix).

review_comments: Ethan Li: Can we expose an override for arena sizes per-cluster? I don't want a single default to cause OOMs on A100-40GB. Maya: Yes, added --arena-size-percent and per-cluster config in runtime/config.md
Priya Shah: Checkpointing looks good but please ensure deterministic seeds for recompute paths in tests. Maya: Added deterministic seed harness in tests and clarified non-determinism caveat in docs.

Connor Blake: Kernel selection scoring needs a weight for latency vs workspace. Did you tune that? Maya: Added latency_estimate into the KernelScore and a runtime knob kernel_score_weights; default favors lower-workspace only under memory pressure.
Rohit Mehra: CI perf failures observed on first run were due to missing CUDA stream sync in arena destructor. Maya: Fixed and re-ran CI; perf matrix now passes.
Ethan Li (approval): Verified in dedicated canary cluster (d-8g-1). Memory savings are real and no regressions observed. Approving to merge.
release_notes: Optimize GPU memory and transient workspace usage: adds optional activation checkpointing, scratch buffer arena pooling, workspace-aware kernel selection, continuous-batching workspace accounting, and KV cache shared region. Opt-in via model and runtime flags. Improves memory headroom for large-context workloads and reduces transient OOMs.
notes_for_ops: Enable --enable-scratch-arena and model.config.enable_workspace_optimizations on a small canary fleet first. Monitor per-GPU arena utilization and tail-latency for recompute-heavy models. Use --arena-size-percent to tune for different GPU SKUs.
post_merge_tasks: Monitor telemetry: memory_headroom, workspace_alloc_failures, tail_latency_p95. Rollout schedule: canary -> staged opt-in -> default changes after 2 weeks of no regressions.
